Operational taxonomic units (OTUs, defined at the 97% sequence similarity level) were picked using the average neighbor method after Needleman alignment and a single-linkage pre-cluster procedure.

steps.evidence: Publicly available data were downloaded using the Sequence Read Archive (SRA) toolkit provided by the NCBI.
the DEBLUR algorithm was used to generate amplicon sequence variants (ASVs).

ASVs from each study (matched to the reference database) were collated in a single biom file and sequences without sequence-level assignments were removed.
Finally, a phylogenetic tree and a biom file with taxonomy were generated using MAFFT and QIIME2, respectively.
Alpha and beta diversity analyses were done with the Vegan package.
Alpha diversity indices used included: rarefied richness, Shannon entropy and Pielou’s evenness.
Beta diversity was observed using Principal Coordinate Analysis (PCoA) with the Weighted Unifrac distance metric.
Analysis of variance in relation to explanatory variables in the metadata was done using Vegan’s Adonis() function with the Weighted Unifrac distance metric.
The core microbiome was determined by identifying taxa with a minimum prevalence of 85% across all samples considered.
Correlation analysis was used to identify potential relationships between abundant genera and selected environmental variables using Kendall correlation
Taxa with significantly differential abundance between groups were visualised using heat trees with a Wilcoxon p-value test
Stochasticity in community assembly was assessed using a Normalized Stochasticity Ratio (NST) with various distance measures
A 50% stochasticity ratio was used to identify more deterministic (<50%) and more stochastic (>50%) assembly.

For the calculations, taxa occurrence frequency and the sample richness were constrained as proportional (P) or fixed (F) in the combinations PF or PP, and 1,000 randomizations were performed for each model.
